code: # Part 1: is the value positive?  Part 2: its level, among the positives. zin_fit <- function(formula, data, ...) {   y <- model.response(model.frame(formula, data = data))   fit_any <- glm(update(formula, I(. > 0) ~ .), family = binomial(), data = data)   fit_pos <- lm(formula, data = data[y > 0, ])   list(any = fit_any, pos = fit_pos) }  zin_sim <- function(model, newdt, ...) {   p_any  <- predict(model$any, newdata = newdt, type = "response")   m_pos  <- predict(model$pos, newdata = newdt)   is_pos <- rbinom(nrow(newdt), 1, p_any)   pos    <- pmax(rnorm(nrow(newdt), m_pos, sigma(model$pos)), 0)   is_pos * pos }  m_zin <- spec_model(   X ~ A + L + time,   var_type   = "custom",   mod_type   = "covariate",   custom_fit = zin_fit,   custom_sim = zin_sim,   truncate   = FALSE   # zin_sim controls its own range )

NULL (default) runs natural course . init_recode recodes applied first time step, models evaluated, e.g. set lags baseline value. in_recode recodes applied start later time step, models evaluated, e.g. update lags. out_recode recodes applied end time step, first included, e.g. advance cumulative counts carry absorbing state forward. mc_sample Number subjects simulated Monte Carlo cohort. default, NULL, uses 50 times number subjects data reports value unless quiet = TRUE. larger value reduces Monte Carlo error, falls 1/sqrt(mc_sample); change estimand. R Number bootstrap replicates (default 500); R = 1 skips bootstrap. Replicates run future.apply::future_lapply: sequentially unless parallel plan set future::plan(), e.g. plan(multisession). future_seed Logical integer.
